newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas surges on impending cold, storage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas surges on impending cold, storage.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices surged by more than 10 cents Tuesday, driven by six- to 10-day forecasts for below-normal temperatures in the East and Midwest, industry sources said.
Sources also attributed the strength to the rally in the futures market and low storage inventories in the producing region and western U.S.
Gulf Coast prices jumped into the high-$2.90s to low-$3 area, up another 10-15 cents from Monday and up about 30 cents from last Tuesday, as a cold front was expected to hit the Northeast Thursday.
In the New York market, prices also gained about 10 cents to the $3.55-3.65 area, with deals reported done as high as $3.75.
Early indications for December 1 delivery at the New York city-gate were $1.25-1.35 over the NYMEX screen, placing the market in the $4.30-4.45 range.

In the Midcontinent, prices were up at least 10 cents to the low-to-mid $2.80s, as buyers turned to the spot market to meet a strong heating demand instead of withdrawing large volumes of gas from storage.
Similarly in south Texas prices rose by about 15 cents to the mid-to-high $2.80s.
In west Texas, tight supplies and effects from the stronger Gulf market pushed Permian prices more than 10 cents higher into the low-to-mid $2.70s.
At the southern California border, traders reported closing deals in the mid-to-high $2.90s, up more than 20 cents on the day and up about 40 cents from November index levels.
Sources attributed the price spike to low storage levels in the West and soaring western Canadian domestic and export prices.
NYMEX's December Henry Hub natural gas futures jumped to a new contract high of $3.17.
